lines.text: The vaults of the Seven went down in rings, like a well. Each level colder than the last, and better guarded.
The first corridor was lined with silver eyes. Tamsin said they were wards. Anyone with a Vessel who walked past them would light them up like a festival, and ring every bell in the cathedral.
So I went first.
I walked the whole length of that corridor. Not one eye so much as blinked. They had been built to catch anything with rings. Nobody had ever thought to build one that caught nothing.
At the far end, every eye ran back to a single stone, cold and humming. I hung my cloak over it. Then the others came through.
I have never been so glad to be with a zero.
The second corridor had men in it. Two Measurers at a crossing, lenses raised, reading everyone who passed.
Tamsin opened two of Tobin's lanterns and rolled them down the floor. White fog poured out of them, thick as milk.
Damp down here. Gets into everything.
Hask had said almost the same words, wiping his lens in my village. It hadn't helped him either.
We walked past them in the fog, close enough to touch. One of them was cleaning his lens on his sleeve. He never looked up.
The third door was iron, with no handle and no lock. Tamsin knocked on it. Four slow, three fast, one slow.
Winter wheat.
A slot opened. A sleepy Measurer peered out at four of us in robes, and one more behind us, much larger.
Why is that dog wearing a robe?
He's a novice.
The sentry looked at Ash for a long time. Ash looked back. Then the sentry decided it was far too early in the morning, and opened the door.
Past the door, Wren stopped us with one hand. The floor ahead was laid in squares, and three of them sat a hair's breadth lower than the rest.
Step where I step. The air moves under those three. Something's waiting.
We stepped where Wren stepped. Nobody breathed.
And then, beyond the next archway, we heard it. Hundreds of people, breathing slowly, all at the same time.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter ninety-six, coming soon.
